 JUDGMENT
This is a suit for permanent injunction and other consequential reliefs.

2. Brief facts of the plaintiffs case is that, the Plaintiff was the tenant under one Sri. Sadiq Patel i.e.,
the father of the Defendants herein in respect of the Shop bearing No. 35, Old No.572/ 6, situated at OTC Road, Cottonpet, Bengaluru, measuring 10 Feet x 13 Feet, totally measuring 130 Sq. Ft., along with rolling shutter, electricity facility and water facility, more vividly described in the Schedule hereunder written and hereinafter referred to as the Schedule Premises.

That originally the Schedule Premises belonged to one Sri. Sadiq Patel i.e., the father of the Defendants herein and earlier the building existing thereon was old and the Plaintiff herein had obtained the Schedule premises on a monthly rent from the father of the Defendants Sri. Sadiq Patel by way of entering into Shop Rent Agreement dated: 05.09.2009 on a monthly rent of Rs. 6,000/- per month and he had paid a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- as advance sale consideration.

That ever since from the date of taking the Schedule Premises on Rent i.e., from September 2009, the Plaintiff herein was running a Tea Stall with Snacks under the name and style of Karnataka Tea Stall and at no point of time the Plaintiff had defaulted in payment of rent and he was regular in the same, such being the factual position, Sri.

Sadiq Patel passed away, leaving behind the Plaintiffs as his heirs to succeed his estate, accordingly the tenancy stood attorned to the defendants and the Plaintiff continued to be tenant under the defendants and the Plaintiff was continuing as a tenant uninterruptedly.
3.

It is further submitted that, when this being the factual position, recently while the adjacent building owner was renovating/ repairing his building premises, since the building existing on the Schedule Premises was old and was in dilapidated condition, the same fell down at that point of time the defendants herein expressed their inability to construct/ renovate the Schedule Premises for want of money and requested the Plaintiff to invest his own money and construct the building on the Schedule Premises and continue in the said premises as tenant therein by paying additional security deposit and increase in the rent.

It is submitted that since the Plaintiff was doing business in the Schedule Premises for more than a decade and the employees therein were entirely depending on the earnings derived in the Schedule Premises for their livelihood, having no other alternative the Plaintiff at his cost and expenses had got renovated/ reconstructed the building on the Schedule Premises and thereafter continued business in the Schedule Premises under the name and style of Karnataka Tea Centre.

It is further submitted that, subsequent to renovating the building on the Schedule Premises,
when the Plaintiff approached the defendants so as to execute Rental Agreement afresh, at that point of time the defendants demanded the Plaintiff to pay additional sum of Rs.4,00,000/- as security deposit and to pay a sum of Rs. 12,000/- as monthly rent, on the demand so made, the Plaintiff having no other alternative agreed for the same with an intention to maintain cordial relationship and upon receipt of the payment, the Defendants executed a fresh Rental Agreement on 27.07.2022 acknowledging to have received a sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- as security deposit which sum includes security deposit of Rs. 1,00,000/ - paid under the Rent Agreement dtd: 05.09.2000 and the Rental Agreement was for a period of Eleven (11) months commencing from 01.08.2022 and it was specifically agreed that the said agreement shall be mutually extended for further period with increased rent by 10% on completion of every eleven months.

That on cursory perusal of the above said facts, it is clear that the Plaintiff is tenant in respect of the Schedule Premises since from the year 2009 and at his own cost and expenses has got the Schedule Property renovated/ reconstructed and that apart has also paid a huge sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- as security deposit, such being the factual position, on 02.11.2023 the defendants herein for the reasons best known by colluding with their men, agents, henchmen with an intention to harass and humiliate the Plaintiff for no fault of him with a sole object of dispossessing the Plaintiff and his employees from the Schedule Premises so as to gain illegally and also to cause wrongful loss to the Plaintiff herein, notwithstanding the fact of the Plaintiff having got the building constructed thereon, but the said act of the defendants, their agents and their henchmen was successfully restrained by the Plaintiff.

5. It is further submitted that, the defendants along with their henchmen, agents and third persons are threatening the plaintiff to dispossess him and his employees from the Schedule Premises by using money and muscle power.
The defendants and their henchmen have scant respect for law and they wield anti-social and political clout and may stoop to any level to see that their illegal designs are put into action.

The defendants in furtherance of their illegal designs had threatened the Plaintiff on 18.11.2023 that unless the Plaintiff vacate the schedule Premises by the end of this month, they would physically throw him out of the Schedule Premises at that point of time the Plaintiff expressed his intention to continue as a tenant therein and also brought to the notice about the fact of the Plaintiff having renovated the building at his own cost and expenses, for which the defendants started acting otherwise and expressed their ill intention to continue the Plaintiff as his tenant and also contrary to the terms of the Agreement.

It is relevant here to state that as per the Agreement, it is clear that the provision for earlier termination is only by way of issuing at least 3 months advance intimating his intention, then only the Defendants are entitled to terminate the agreement and take repossession of the Premises and that there is a specific clause of renewing the Agreement for a further period, but in the present case on hand at no point of time the Plaintiff has committed default.

6. It is further submitted that, he is a tenant under the Defendants and the Rental Agreement dated:
01.08.2022 so entered between the parties has not been terminated and the defendants have been accepting the rents without any protest, further at no point of time the Defendant has issued any prior notice as envisaged under law, such being the factual position, the Plaintiff has all rights to continue in the Schedule premises without any hindrance from the defendants or their henchmen,

trespass and threaten the Plaintiff of dire consequences without following due process of law, but the said act of defendant and his henchmen was successfully restrained by the Plaintiff and his family members.

Whether the plaintiff is entitled for the relief of perpetual injunction by restraining the Defendants, their agents, servants, henchmen, family members, any one acting under them or claiming through them, from dispossessing the Plaintiff from the schedule premises or any part thereof, and / or in any way interfere with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the schedule premises by the Plaintiffs, without due process of law ?
4. What order or decree ?
opennyai_summary.decision:
The defendants stated that they have issued notice for eviction as per Ex.D.1 and they proceed as per law.
Hence I answered Issue Nos.1 to 3 in the affirmative.
In view of the findings on the above issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following :
O R D E R
The suit filed by the plaintiff is hereby decreed with costs.
It is hereby ordered that, the defendants, their agents, servants, henchmen, family members, any one acting under them or claiming through them are hereby restrained by issue of permanent injunction from dispossessing the plaintiff from the schedule premises or any part thereof, and / or in any way interfering with the plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment over the schedule premises without due process of law.
Draw decree accordingly.
